changes.after: A Struct can supply ways to read and write its fields. A Data object here supplies a reader without a writer.

before: Struct.new(:title) creates a class with a title reader and writer. Data.define(:title) creates a value-like class with a reader but no member writer. Assigning these classes to constants gives them useful names.

Data instances are immutable containers, but mutable members are not automatically frozen. A Data member holding an array can still expose changes to that array. Choose immutable members or explicit copying/freezing when the whole value must stay stable.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
Draft = Struct.new(:title)
Published = Data.define(:title)
draft = Draft.new("map")
published = Published.new("map")
draft.title = "atlas"
puts draft.title
puts published.title
```

Expected output or behavior: atlas
map. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
